subject: Aurora Diagnostics — Post-call: Eval runbook, dataset spec & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@auroradx.com>, Emily Turner <emily.turner@auroradx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aurora Diagnostics — Post-call: Eval runbook, dataset spec & next steps

Hi Sanjay / Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we can get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood this week.

What we heard
- Primary goal: automated triage summarization + suggestion of next test codes from clinical notes. High precision required on code recommendations (low false positives).
- Target latency: sub-400ms p50 for single-note inference in a dedicated path.
- Data: you can share de-identified notes (PHI removed) for closed eval.

Recommended models to start (balanced perf/cost)
- redwood/clarity-7b-q4: baseline — fast, low-cost; good for throughput tests.
- redwood/clarity-13b-q4o: primary quality candidate for accuracy benchmarks.
- redwood/ozone-70b-fp16 (fallback): for edge cases in human evals where higher capacity is needed.

Quick eval plan (high level)
1) You provide a 200–500 sample CSV (attached: aurora_sample_dataset_v1.csv) with columns: id, note_text, ground_truth_codes (comma-separated), expected_action, confidence_band (high/med/low), source_date.
2) Redwood will run model inference (same prompt set) across the recommended model variants and produce per-example outputs + automated scoring metrics.
3) Scoring: exact code match recall/precision, top-1/top-3 accuracy, normalized Levenshtein for free-text suggestions, and a small human eval pool (20 examples) for clinical acceptability.
4) Deliverable: a runbook + leaderboard (per-model metrics), failure-mode examples, and prompt recommendations.

Privacy & delivery notes
- If you prefer S3: provide a pre-signed upload URL. If not, a Drive share is fine (we’ll pull into a private bucket). Data will be stored in your region for the eval and removed after 30 days unless you request otherwise.

Next steps / asks (actionable)
- Sanjay: share the sample CSV and a short list of 10 canonical prompts you currently use (by EOD Wed).
- Emily: confirm whether we should use your US or EU data region (defaulting to US).
- Ben / Marissa: can you confirm a short internal window for dedicated capacity (we typically provision a 4-hour slot for the 13B runs)?

Attached: aurora_sample_dataset_v1.csv (sample format) and a 1-page quickstart (aurora-eval-quickstart.pdf) with upload instructions and the scoring schema.

I’ll follow up with a short runbook once we get the sample.

Thanks — Priyom

Subject: Re: Aurora Diagnostics — Post-call: Eval runbook, dataset spec & next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching our sanitized sample (attached here as aurora_sample_dataset_v1.csv). A few quick clarifications: 

1) Scoring thresholds — what do you typically recommend as a go/no-go? For code recommendations our internal bar is 95% precision on top-1 for high-confidence cases. Is that realistic for the 13B you suggested?

2) Data handling — we need an explicit confirmation that the eval data will not be used for model training or shared across other tenants. Also need SOC2 evidence for the storage process (happy to get an NDA addendum if needed).

3) Timing — the team prefers Thursday morning for the first run (we have clinicians available for the small human eval pool Friday).

If you confirm the storage & isolation terms above, we’ll mark the sample as ready and drop the Drive link in a follow-up.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Clinical AI, Aurora Diagnostics
sanjay.rao@auroradx.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Diagnostics — Post-call: Eval runbook, dataset spec & next steps

Thanks Sanjay — quick answers inline and expanded runbook steps below.

On thresholds
- 95% top-1 precision on high-confidence examples is aggressive but achievable for clear-cut mapping examples with the 13B variant if your ground truth labels are well-formed. For ambiguous notes we typically see lower precision and recommend reporting top-3 recall + a precision at confidence threshold.

On data handling & compliance
- Confirmed: eval data for this engagement will be isolated to a dedicated private bucket in your chosen region and will NOT be used to train or fine-tune public models. We can attach a short amendment to the MSA stating that explicitly.
- I’ve cc’d Ben and Marissa for SOC2 artifacts; Ben will share our SOC2 evidence bundle and our retention/audit timeline.

Runbook (detailed steps we will execute)
1) Data ingestion (T0) — You upload the CSV to the Drive folder (or provide an S3 presigned URL). We validate format and run a quick schema check (id, note_text, ground_truth_codes).
2) Prep & canonicalization (T0 + 2h) — Our data team normalizes codes to your canonical codebook (we’ll ask for mapping if it differs).
3) Prompt set application (T0 + 3h) — We run a fixed prompt set (attached in drive link) across the models. Prompts include: system instructions, examples for mapping, and a short-chain-of-thought instruction for ambiguous cases.
4) Automated scoring (T0 + 4h) — Metrics computed: precision@1 (by confidence band), recall@3, macro-F1 for multi-code cases, mean normalized edit distance for free-text suggestions.
5) Human review (T0 + 6–8h) — Clinician pool reviews 20 flagged borderline examples and assigns accept/reject.
6) Delivery (T0 + 10h) — Deliverable: runbook PDF, model leaderboard CSV, and a short primer on prompt tuning steps if you want to iterate.

Operational notes
- Dedicated capacity: for the 13B runs we recommend a 4-hour slot; we can compress the schedule if you need quicker turnaround but cost will increase.
- Regression watch: we’ll run the same prompts and the same seed/config to ensure deterministic runs across candidates. If we later re-run (post-deploy) we record model and runtime hashes and push regression alerts to your team.

Attachments & links
- I uploaded the runbook skeleton and the canonical prompt set to the Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroEvalPlaybook).
- Ben — can you drop the SOC2 packet link into the thread?

If Thursday morning still works for you we’ll schedule the dedicated slot and send a calendar invite.

Cheers — Priyom

- Ops (Karthik): provision a 4-hour dedicated 13B slot on Thu 2026-11-12 09:00–13:00 PT, region: us-west-2. Confirm GPU profile and estimated token budget.
- Compliance (Ben): please share the SOC2 evidence bundle link and confirm the data retention hook (delete after 30 days by default). Ben is cc’d above — can you post the link into the external thread after you validate?

Prompt + dataset notes for the run

Customer asks to confirm non-training usage and isolation — we will include the amendment in the DocuSign packet if needed.

I’ll schedule the invite once Karthik confirms capacity.

Thanks — Priyom
